French cultural centre. Here you will find a café, library and often times there are concerts, films and art exhibitions.
Built in 1834.
The national park preserves a wilderness area around the hill known as Cerro El Veladero. Near the Colonia Palma Sola is a rocky area with prehistoric petroglyphs carved on 18 granite boulders.
On the banks of the river (near the city stadium), this 5.6 acres of parkland offer a pleasant and relaxing environment to stroll or to sit and watch the river flow by.
The mysterious sea road where the sea water splits, or Ganjo Yukgye-do, is 1 km south, and there are many tourist attractions such as Unlimsanbang, Ssanggyesa Temple, and Yongjangsanseong Fortress.
Built in 1987 in retro style on the site of an earlier mosque.
Indoor swimming facilities, including water slide, swimming pool, hot water pool and diving towers. Next door there are several other rather dry sports facilities. Open all year.
Monastery belonging to the Greek-Melkite Catholic Church.
It was founded in 2008 by Frashad Kamalkhani, the museum owner. It includes a collection of early office machines.
Honors the men and women from Kazakhstan who died in World War II. There's an eternal flame by the war memorial.
A large water park near Tagarades Hill. Free bus service starting at the city centre.
A symbol of the city of Chimoio and a "must" for dedicated travellers. The hill resembles the head of an old man. It is not a terribly high climb but offers a nice view of the city.

Among Milan's oldest (founded in the 16th century), but quite small gardens, and are very close to the University district. The parks, however, were only opened to the public in the early 20th century.
Mountain peak Ćurevac is a great point for panoramic mountain views.
It is the highest mountain of all Adriatic islands. It has a great view of the Zlatni Rat beach, place Bol and islands Hvar and Vis.
The voestalpine steel works run an impressive museum and experience centre devoted to the manufacturing and processing of steel, as well as applications thereof.
Urfa is believed to have been the birthplace of the Prophet Abraham (İbrahim in Turkish and Arabic) and so is an important Islamic place of pilgrimage.
It's now the symbol of Palic, was built at the beginning of the 20th century as a multipurpose facility: a water tower, gate of the resort and a tram station.

There's been a substantial Jewish community in Bukhara since the 8th century. This synagogue was built around 1640, in legend as part of the peace deal with the widow who owned the Lyab-i Hauz site.
Behind Neve Zohar you can find interesting canyons and further up the archaeological site and fortress Metsad Zohar.
Shimal Fort, known locally as 'Sheba's Palace', the remains of an Islamic era fortification.

One of the most important galleries in the country, the WHAG houses a collection of traditional and contemporary South African graphics, sculptures and paintings. It hosts many special exhibitions from time to time.
Its west and south walls are still visible.
Climb this hill for a great view of the underlying royal palace and the city.

Plage de Sal Sal to the north of the city is pristine and deserted, so much that you might not encounter anyone else here. The beach stretches across the border to Mauritania, so you should be careful not to go too far north.
Dilapidated amusement park. Has some old water rides and rollercoasters.
Next to the pleasant river bank.

items.d: Real baroque houses. The quarter reaches from the "Heinrichstraße" up to the "Albert Platz". On the Heinrichstr and in the surroundings you will find a lot of antique stores.
Here you can walk around looking at relics of military prowess.

A stone plaque commemorating the shooting down of a US Navy (not "USAF" as depicted) aircraft in 1967. Read the Vietnamese script and you can pick out the name of John McCain, the late U.S. senator, one of the airmen.

While the Royal Palace is in Stockholm's Old Town, the Royal family lives at Drottningholm Palace on the Lovön island in Lake Mälaren. The 18th-century palace is beautiful, and much of it is open to the public.
This mosque with a very beautiful and interesting architecture is included in the list of 30 most unique mosques in the world.
An ancient convent where you can see the uncomfortable stone slabs where nuns slept, religious artwork, and, most importantly, a creepy underground crypt filled with mummified nuns.

Considered to be one of the oldest temples of Khajuraho made entirely in granite and sandstone, is dedicated to Vishnu.
The largest mosque in Quba, also made of bricks and multicoloured, was built in the early 19th century by Haji Jeffer.
